## Appearance

Aunt Martha is seventy-five years old and suffers from failing sight, leaving her nearly blind. In addition to her poor vision, she is extremely hard of hearing.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P25](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0025), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008)_

## Personality

Aunt Martha is an elderly, ill-tempered, and irritable woman who frequently exhibits a crabby demeanor. She is a remarkably poor housekeeper and an erratic laundress, though she remains firmly determined to hold total control over the food supply. Despite her difficult temperament, she possesses skill in knitting.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P25](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0025), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P0](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER V. ## History

Aunt Martha was raised seven decades in the past in a strict, traditional manner, an approach she intended to pass on to others. After [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) took up residence in the manse, Aunt Martha sparred with her over food. She later became bedridden, leaving the children to manage the house in her absence. On one occasion, Aunt Martha killed the children's pet rooster, [Adam](../character/adam.md), to serve for dinner to a visiting minister.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P8](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P9](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0009), [v5 CHAPTER VI. ## Quotes

> "Do not go disturbing your unfortunate father, as his worries are already sufficient, and I serve as the housekeeper in this place."
>
> — Aunt Martha — [v5 CHAPTER XIX. POOR ADAM! P3](../source/v05-c19.md#nw-v05-c19-p0003)

> "You are far too grown-up to cause such a commotion about an aged rooster. You were aware that he would need to be slaughtered eventually."
>
> — Aunt Martha — [v5 CHAPTER XIX. POOR ADAM! P1](../source/v05-c19.md#nw-v05-c19-p0001)

> "Blessedly, John is absent. Cold boiled meat and bread exist in abundance, and attempting to prepare porridge is something you can try."
>
> — Aunt Martha — [v5 CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE P11](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0011)

> "Until I can manage to move about, you have to keep struggling,"
>
> — Aunt Martha — [v5 CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE P11](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0011)

> "What foolishness are you young rips up to now?"
>
> — Aunt Martha — [v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY P5](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0005)

## Relationships

### [Grace](../character/grace.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/aunt-martha--grace.md)

Aunt Martha is the aunt of [Grace](../character/grace.md). While Aunt Martha is bedridden, [Grace](../character/grace.md) and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) try to step in to clean the house, which accidentally results in a village scandal when they beat carpets in the cemetery on a Sunday. Aunt Martha also causes [Grace](../character/grace.md) great heartbreak by slaughtering Grace's pet rooster to serve to a visiting minister.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P17](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0017), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P91](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0091), [v5 CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE P10](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0010), +7 more_

### [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/aunt-martha--john-ashdown.md)

Aunt Martha is a relative of [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md), serving as an aunt within the household. She manages household responsibilities alongside him, though his absorption in theology leads to general neglect of the family and reliance on Aunt Martha's presence.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. HECTOR TWISS MAKES A CALL P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. HECTOR TWISS MAKES A CALL P15](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0015), [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. HECTOR TWISS MAKES A CALL P21](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0021), +2 more_

### [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/aunt-martha--rupert.md)
